Case: Mattie is a 75-year-old with history of lung cancer and 4 months of progressive low-back and right leg pain. Mattie describes the pain as a dull ache that shoots down his right leg in no particular pattern or frequency. Recently, he started experiencing intermittent numbness throughout his right leg. Overall, he believes the pain is becoming more frequent and intolerable, as it now interrupts his sleep nightly and acetaminophen and ibuprofen have not helped. On your physical examination, you find that Mattie has diffusely diminished sensation in his leg, but his strength and reflexes are normal. Question: Would you offer morphine to Mattie? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
